provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-01, Larry's son asking the four cold interview probes written the same day and typing Larry's answers as he spoke them. Nothing from the day's document research was supplied to him before he answered. Raw capture and analysis: research/interviews/2026-09-01-phone-answers.md.
text: Special Forces ran the camp. Captain Kennedy was in Charge of the camp most of the time. But I really worked for 1st Cavalry
researchNotes: Answer to a probe asking only who was in charge at the camp, with no name, rank or initial supplied. Two things follow. First, Captain Kennedy moves from a man tentatively identified in VN-0006 and credited with taking VN-0023 to, in Larry's words, the man in charge of the camp most of the time. Second, the RADIX Press order of battle read hours earlier lists a 1LT Lewis commanding at Núi Bà Đen from 20 April 1965 (sources/radix-sf-order-of-battle); Larry did not say Lewis. The difference is left standing rather than reconciled — a detachment commander of record and the man Larry experienced as running the place need not be the same, and TDY rotations through this site were constant. "But I really worked for 1st Cavalry" is his most direct statement yet of the 1st Cavalry association, and still sits against the division's arrival in country around September 1965.
